advanced_search.description: Search with xeno-canto's own search tags, for anything Search recordings has no filter for: background species, remarks, recording method, equipment, sample rate, coordinates, annotations and more. Each term is a tag and a value, such as cnt:brazil or q:A, and every term must match.

parameters.description: A query in xeno-canto's search tags: each term a tag, a colon and a value, with double quotes around a value of several words or with an operator, as in sp:"larus fuscus" cnt:netherlands len:"<30". Every term must match. The tags are listed at https://xeno-canto.org/help/search. A value xeno-canto would silently ignore for type, sex, stage or method is refused.

recording.remarks: High and low pass filtering in post, but not so as to affect recorded vocalisation.  Time intervals between song bursts are as recorded.  20 m to the bird singing from low cover and from a low fence.  No other wrens singing close by.  Longer and other recordings of the same individual are available as .wav/.flac.  Clear, calm but cool conditions.

search_recordings.description: Search xeno-canto's recordings by species, English or scientific name, and by group, country, world area, sound type, sex, life stage, quality rating, length, year recorded, upload date, recordist and licence, best rated first. Returns each recording's details, audio and sonogram links, licence and citation, with how many recordings and species match.

parameters.description: The species to find, by English name (Eurasian Wren) or scientific name (Troglodytes troglodytes); or a subspecies (Larus fuscus graellsii), genus (Larus) or family (Laridae). Part of an English name finds every species whose name contains it: wren finds all the wrens. English names are xeno-canto's, which follow the IOC list for birds, so Turdus merula is the Common Blackbird. Also takes a recording from another xeno-canto step, to find more of its species.

description: Search xeno-canto, a community collection of more than a million wildlife sound recordings from around the world: birds, grasshoppers and crickets, bats, frogs and land mammals. Find recordings of a species by English or scientific name, filtered by country, sound type, quality rating, length, date and licence; find recordings made near a place; draw one at random; get a recording's details, sonograms and annotations; and download its audio. Needs a free xeno-canto API key.
